title: Korean Beef and Sweet Potato Glass Noodle Stir-Fry
summary: A dairy-free Korean-style japchae-inspired lunch with springy sweet potato-style glass noodles, savoury beef, mushrooms and colourful vegetables. It is lightly sweet, garlicky and glossy with sesame and soy flavours.

ingredients.name: rice noodles, used in place of sweet potato glass noodles

steps: Cook the rice noodles according to the packet instructions until just tender and springy, then drain and rinse briefly under cool water. Snip the noodles a few times with scissors if they are very long, then set aside.
In a bowl, mix the beef with 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 0.5 tbsp brown sugar, half the garlic, the ginger and the black pepper. Leave to marinate while you prepare the vegetables.
Stir together the remaining soy sauce, remaining sesame oil, remaining brown sugar and remaining garlic to make the finishing sauce.

Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add the onion, carrot and red pepper with the salt, then stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until the vegetables are bright and just beginning to soften. Transfer to a large bowl.
Add the shiitake mushrooms to the pan and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes until softened and lightly browned, then add them to the bowl with the vegetables.
Add the spinach to the pan with a splash of water and cook for 1 minute until just wilted. Squeeze off any excess liquid if needed, then add to the bowl.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil in the pan. Add the marinated beef in a single layer and stir-fry for 2–3 minutes until browned on the outside and just cooked through.
Add the cooked noodles, vegetables and finishing sauce to the pan with the beef. Toss over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until everything is hot, glossy and evenly coated.
Remove from the heat, toss through the spring onions and sesame seeds, then taste and adjust with a little more soy sauce or sesame oil if desired before serving.
